title: HapticMessage
description: OPUS Haptic Protocol (see contracts/HAPTIC_PROTOCOL.md, v1.2). One JSON datagram per message, UDP 8790 (game->node, node replies on the same socket) and UDP 8791 (node discovery broadcast). TWO MESSAGE FAMILIES share this schema; a message is valid when it matches EITHER: (1) '#/$defs/internalV1': the game's internal v1 envelope, which always carries v:1, id and ts_ms (cue, stop, config, ping, status, ack, imu); (2) '#/$defs/wire': device-level wire messages as the firmware and Node B emit them, which do NOT carry v/id/ts_ms (device_discovery, the legacy opus_haptic hello, sensor_data, sensor_chunk, emg_burst, display, subscribe, status, ack). Firmware v0.5.0 deliberately emits status and ack with both dialects merged in one packet (v/id/ts_ms/ack_id/ok AND cue_id/status/timestamp_ms), so those match both families; that is fine because the top level is anyOf. The haptic DEVICE COMMAND (motor/intensity/duration_ms/pattern, optional cue 'stroke' and play_at_ms) is a separate schema: haptic-device-command.schema.json.

internalV1.description: Family 1: internal v1 envelope. Requires v, type, id, ts_ms.

battery_pct.description: null when the node runs from a power bank (no battery sense)

unknown_msgs.description: v1.2: ignored message types since boot

wire.description: Family 2: device-level wire messages (no v/id/ts_ms). Matches when ANY member matches.

deviceDiscovery.description: PRD v2 section 9.1. Broadcast to UDP 8791 every 1000 ms by Node A (device_kind haptic, motor_count 2) and Node B (device_kind bio, motor_count 0). Node A's packet also carries the legacy hello fields (opus_haptic, port) and extra fields (device_name, protocol_version, ip, motor_channels), which are allowed.

legacyHello.description: The original discovery hello the Unity HapticClient parses: {"opus_haptic":1,"device_id":...,"port":8790,"fw":...}. No 'type' field. Node A still emits these fields inside its device_discovery packet.

sensorData.description: Node A sensor_data v1: 100 Hz, ONE sample per packet, RAW units (accel m/s2, gyro rad/s). Keys: imu_accel_x/y/z (required in practice), imu_gyro_x/y/z and imu_temperature may also be present; consumers must tolerate extra sensor names, so additionalProperties stays open.

sensorChunk.description: Node B (bio) EMG stream, PRD v2 section 9.3: every 100 ms, up to 10 envelope values at 100 Hz. The array may be shorter than 10 (the PRD example shows 4) but never longer.

timestamp_ms.description: device clock (millis()) of the FIRST sample in the chunk (manager decision); sample i is at timestamp_ms + i * 1000 / sample_rate_hz

sample_rate_hz.description: envelope rate; 100 for Node B v0.5.0

emgBurst.description: Node B: envelope above baseline + 3 SD for at least 30 ms.

timestamp_ms.description: device clock (millis()) at burst ONSET (manager decision)

peak.description: peak envelope value, same unit as sensor_chunk (raw_adc)

display.description: Game -> Node A: one line of OLED text. At most 12 characters, at most 2 per second. v0.2.1: the electronics team's firmware reads `mode`, the reference firmware and the twin read `text`; the game sends both with the same value, and either one alone is valid.

mode.description: same line as `text` (electronics team dialect), e.g. SYNC / ASYNC

subscribe.description: Any device -> Node A or B: register for sensor/status packets. Resend at least every 2 s; a subscriber expires after 5 s; at most 3 live subscribers per node.

keepalive.description: v0.2.1. Game -> Node A or B, about once per second: feeds the firmware's 2 s motor watchdog and (electronics team firmware) marks the sender as the telemetry target. Sent in addition to ping and subscribe; nodes that do not know it ignore it.

deviceStatus.description: Node status without the v1 envelope. Firmware v0.5.0 also adds v/id/ts_ms/motors_ok/imu_ok/fw (then it matches internalV1 too).

deviceAck.description: Node ack in the Electronics-contract dialect (cue_id + status). Firmware v0.5.0 also adds ack_id and ok. v0.2.1: the electronics team's firmware sends `accepted` (boolean) instead of `status`; false means the cue was NOT played (motor busy, 100 ms gap, duty budget, invalid motor/intensity) and must be recorded as not delivered.
